Title: Finish one clean Windows build end to end
Description: Run scripts/build-windows.ps1 on the owner's PC. Done when SoundwaveAI-Setup-<version>.exe exists, installs, and Settings -> Voice & Desktop shows that version.

Title: Install the build on a clean Windows machine
Description: A PC with no Node, no Python, no ffmpeg - the claim the product makes. Check clip export, voice input, YouTube import, and no Defender quarantine. desktop\bin carries ffmpeg + yt-dlp + whisper.cpp + the MSVC runtime for exactly this.

Title: Buy a Windows code-signing certificate
Description: OV approx $200-400/yr. Until then every install says Unknown publisher and SmartScreen fights the customer. CI env vars are already wired and sign when present - this is a purchase, not a task.

Title: Publish a release and prove auto-update works
Description: Publish with -PublishTag v1.6.7, put latest.yml + setup exe in the soundwave-updates feed repo, install the PREVIOUS version on a test machine and watch it update. Never run end to end: CI was billing-blocked and no local test covers the download.

Title: Create SOUNDWAVE_UPDATE_TOKEN and SOUNDWAVE_UPDATE_REPO
Description: GitHub secret + repository variable that the release workflow and the feed publish step read. Needed before auto-update can be exercised.

Title: Add a -PublishFeed switch to the build script
Description: One run publishes installers AND the feed files (latest.yml + setup exe) instead of two manual uploads. Offered during the build work, not built.

Title: Decide the CI question
Description: GitHub Actions is blocked by account billing (steps: [], 'recent account payments have failed'). Options: fix Settings -> Billing and plans; make the repo public for free Windows runners; a third-party runner; own-PC builds only. Own-PC works today, but CI is the only other place a Windows installer has ever been built.

Title: Set Stripe live keys and price IDs
Description: STRIPE_PRICE_PRO_MONTHLY/ANNUAL, STRIPE_PRICE_ENTERPRISE_*, STRIPE_PRICE_LIFETIME, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Today /billing/plans reports lifetime.reason=no_price: the $199 Founder tier is coded and cannot be bought.

Title: One real purchase end to end in live mode
Description: Checkout -> webhook -> plan flips -> metering reflects it. Include a refund path. Anything broken between checkout and metering is invisible until money moves.

Title: Verify the Founder seat counter
Description: Confirm sold increments past each purchase and the 101st attempt gets the 409 'sold out'. FOUNDER_SEATS=100.

Title: Verify grandfathering with a back-dated account
Description: PRICING_CHANGED_AT=2026-10-06: anyone who subscribed before that keeps their old terms. Test with a back-dated subscription.

Title: Generate the Prisma migration for the new columns
Description: subscriptionStartedAt, videoMinutesUsed, clipsUsed and the lifetime fields are in server/prisma/schema.prisma with NO migration file - production would not have them. prisma migrate diff is unusable in the build sandbox (binaries.prisma.sh TLS failure), so generate it where Prisma can reach its binaries. Done when prisma migrate deploy adds the columns to a copy of production.

Title: Deploy the landing and pricing pages
Description: frontend/src/pages/Landing.tsx and Pricing.tsx are written and deliberately unrouted (see the note at the top of each). They need a static host and a deploy hook, or the 'Your footage never leaves your PC' pitch exists only in the repo.

Title: Re-verify every price on the landing pages before they go up
Description: The figures were read in October 2026 and competitor pricing moves. The $106/mo stack table and the '3 vs 7 days' retention claim are the two most likely to age badly.

Title: Confirm the Gemini key path in the first-run wizard
Description: The wizard sends people to AI Studio for a free key. Confirm it works for someone with no AI Studio account at all.

Title: Confirm nothing in the publish path burns YouTube quota on reads
Description: 10,000 units/day, 1,600 per upload. Fine for one or two uploads per user per day, but reads could eat it.

Title: Revisit Soundwave's own Google OAuth client for the sold build
Description: There is a product-level decision in docs/COMPETITIVE-PLAN.md to skip it; the fallback (paste your own client once) is honest and works. Revisit if buyers complain.

Title: Defender false positive on first run
Description: assemble.mjs protects the staged server on purpose, which is what a heuristic scanner flags. If customers hit it the answer is the signing certificate, not a weaker protection step.

Title: Microsoft Store listing (optional distribution)
Description: Needs the signing certificate first, and its own copy review.
